html:
The Wandjina are the cloud and rain spirits of Aboriginal peoples of the north-west Kimberley in Western Australia, painted in rock shelters as large white figures with dark eyes, a halo-like headdress and no mouth.

They belong to the law of the Worrorra, Ngarinyin and Wunambal, and of neighbours such as the Gaambera and Kwini. In the Dreaming the Wandjina came from sky and sea, made the land and its people, and brought the wet season rains. When their work was done they lay down in the rock shelters and became the paintings, each tied to a place and a clan.

Custodians repaint them to renew their power. The oldest Wandjina art is thought to be about 4,000 years old. The figures remain central to Kimberley Aboriginal identity.
sum: The Wandjina are the cloud and rain spirits of Aboriginal peoples of the north-west Kimberley in Western Australia, painted in rock shelters as large white figures with dark eyes, a halo-like headdress and no mouth.
